## Description

A cell of the connective tissue of the dermis, in culture: spindle-shaped (~130 × 30 µm spread,
~3000 µm³), stuck to the bottom, it migrates with a lamellipodium and stops when it touches another
(contact inhibition). It stops dividing when the monolayer is complete.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).
<!-- /GENERATED -->

The reference [animal cell](../../mechanics/animal-cells.md): persistent random walk, contact inhibition of
locomotion and proliferation, restriction point (serum), G0, glucose/glutamine Michaelis–Menten uptake
and ~1 lactate per glucose. Validated: doubling time, Fürth MSD and the confluence plateau.

## Literature

- Young-donor human dermal fibroblasts in DMEM + 10 % FBS: population doubling ~24–48 h (central
  value used).
- Gail M.H., Boone C.W. (1970) The locomotion of mouse fibroblasts in tissue culture. Biophys. J. 10:
  980–993 (persistent random walk).
- Alberts B. et al. *Molecular Biology of the Cell*, 6th ed., fig. 17-4 (S 8 h, G2 4 h, M 1 h of a typical human cell).
- Carruthers A. (1990) Facilitated diffusion of glucose. Physiol. Rev. 70: 1135–1176 (GLUT1 Km ~1–3 mM).

## Not implemented yet

- No senescence (Hayflick limit) or passage counter.
- No extracellular matrix secretion.
- No phase-contrast lens yet: cultures are seen in bright field (roadmap C).
- Not supported in the well-mixed culture.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Defines the [animal-cell mechanisms](../../mechanics/animal-cells.md) shared with NIH/3T3, HaCaT and HeLa.
